title: Costs roll up daily by site and worker type
description:
Per-job costs answer "what did this clip cost." Operators ask "what did last
month cost, and which site drove it." That is an aggregate, and it must not be
computed by scanning the jobs table at read time.

`_get_admin_overview` currently derives every KPI from `_jobs.scan(Limit=100)`.
That is already the defect in auritus-294fa6, where a 25-item page silently
omitted the newest job in the system. A partial scan produces a cost total
that looks authoritative and is simply wrong -- worse than one that is visibly
incomplete, because nothing signals the shortfall.

Rollups are written incrementally on completion and read directly.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Daily cost rollups

  Scenario: A completed Batch job adds to the daily rollup
    Given the daily rollup for a site is empty
    When a Batch job for that site completes with a GPU cost
    Then the daily rollup gpu cost equals that job cost
    And the daily rollup batch job count is one

  Scenario: A local job adds platform cost but no GPU cost
    Given the daily rollup for a site is empty
    When a local job for that site completes
    Then the daily rollup gpu cost is zero
    And the daily rollup local job count is one

  Scenario: Rollups separate sites
    Given jobs complete for site "site-a" and site "site-b"
    Then each site has its own daily rollup

  Scenario: Rollups are read without scanning the jobs table
    Given thirty days of rollups exist for a site
    When the operator requests the cost summary for that site
    Then the summary is read from the rollup records

  Scenario: A regenerated job adds its new cost without erasing the old
    Given a job completed with a GPU cost yesterday
    When the job is regenerated and completes again today
    Then yesterday's rollup is unchanged
    And today's rollup includes the new cost
```

That last scenario is the interesting one: regeneration (auritus-907209, in
the M10 epic) means a single content hash can incur cost more than once. Cost
belongs to the *completion event*, not to the job record -- otherwise
regenerating a clip silently rewrites history.

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/stacks/backend.py`** -- a new `AuritusCostRollups` table:

- Partition key `rollup_key` (`f"{site_id}#{date}"`), sort key or plain
  attributes for the measures.
- Attributes: `gpu_cost_usd`, `platform_cost_usd`, `batch_job_count`,
  `local_job_count`, `billed_seconds`, `local_duration_seconds`.
- `PAY_PER_REQUEST`, `RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`, consistent with the other tables.
- No TTL. Cost history is the one thing that should outlive its jobs -- the
  M10 retention story (auritus-e45264) will expire job records, and the
  rollups must survive that or every retention pass destroys the cost record.

**Writes** -- `update_item` with `ADD` on the numeric attributes, so
concurrent completions accumulate atomically rather than racing a
read-modify-write. Both `_mark_done`/`_mark_failed` (platform cost, local
duration) and the batch telemetry Lambda (GPU cost, billed seconds) write to
the same rollup; `ADD` makes that safe without coordination.

**Idempotency** -- EventBridge delivers at least once, so the telemetry
Lambda can fire twice for one Batch job and double-count. Guard it: record
the processed Batch job ID on the job record and make the rollup write
conditional on not having seen it. This is the single most likely source of
wrong numbers in the whole epic.

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`** -- `GET /admin/costs` with optional
`site_id`, `from`, and `to`, returning daily rows plus a total. Query the
rollup table by key range; never scan.

## Blocked on

The per-job estimated cost story, which supplies the figures being summed.
